rationale: The agent correctly verified the user’s identity via full name and ZIP, worked only on the authenticated user’s orders, and used the tools appropriately to look up orders and product variants. It also handled the watch modification properly by asking for and receiving explicit confirmation before making the change. However, the agent made two order-changing writes without explicit confirmation: (1) it updated the shipping address for pending order #W6729841 to the address from order #W3445693 immediately after the user specified the source order, without restating the exact change and obtaining explicit confirmation to proceed; and (2) it initiated the exchange of the delivered air purifier in order #W3445693 to the large, HEPA, night-mode variant without first confirming the exact exchange and any associated charges. Policy requires explicit confirmation before any change. Therefore, despite largely correct tool use and outcomes, the process violated the confirmation requirement, so it does not meet the pass bar.
